 -2-  MFA No. 1153 of 2017  THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 06.10.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.347/14 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MACT, UDUPI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 06.10.2016 passed in MVC No.347/2014 by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member Additional MACT, Udupi, whereby the petition came to be allowed in part and a sum of Rs.7,61,068/- has been awarded as compensation holding that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 therein are liable to pay compensation, the petitioner has approached this Court in appeal seeking enhancement urging various grounds.
2. The parties would be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. The facts relevant for the purpose of this appeal are as below:
It is the case of the appellant that on 03.01.2014 at about 7.00 a.m., he being a pillion rider of a two wheeler was hit by a Lorry bearing No.TN-37/AT-6305.

As a result, the rider of the two wheeler fell down and succumbed to the injuries, whereas the appellant was a pillion rider got injured and shifted to TMA Pai Hospital and then KMC Hospital, Manipal.

The petitioner contended that he had sustained disability to his upper limb as well as lower limb and he was doing Centering work as a construction labourer and due to the injuries sustained by him he has been disabled and is suffering from functional disability also.
It was contended that he had to spend huge amount for the treatment and as such he may be granted adequate compensation by the Tribunal.
The petitioner also contended that the offending Lorry was insured by respondent No.2 owned by respondent No.1 and as such, the respondents are liable to compensate the petitioner.
4. On issuance of notice by the tribunal, respondent No.2/insurance company appeared and respondent No.1/ owner of the Lorry did not appear before the Tribunal.

The insurance company opposed the petition on the ground that there was no such actionable negligence on the part of the Dinesh Poojary vs Jailpuddin S on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142092064/
2 Lorry driver and the accident was due to the negligence of two wheeler rider.

It was also contended that the policy was issued subject to certain terms and conditions and such terms and conditions were violated by the driver and owner of the Lorry and as such, it is not liable to pay the compensation and prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings and contentions of the parties, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues for its consideration and tried the matter along with connected MVC No.348/2014 which was arising out of the death of the rider of two wheeler.
Before the Tribunal, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1, got examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P.31.
Respondents placed policy copy and did not adduce oral evidence.

6. On hearing both the sides and considering the materials available on record, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition against respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and awarded a sum of Rs.7,61,068/- as compensation under different heads and as under:
1 Pain and suffering Rs. 1,00,000/-
2 Loss of future income Rs. 2,00,000/-
3 Medical Expenses Rs. 4,11,068/-
4 Loss of income during laid up period Rs. 30,000/- 5 Food and nourishment and incidental Rs 20,000/-
expenses Total Rs.7,61,068/-
7.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the appellant/petitioner is before this Court in appeal seeking enhancement.

8. On issuance of notice the respondent/insurance company has appeared before this Court and notice to respondent No.1/owner was dispensed with at the risk of the appellant and the Tribunal records have been secured.

9. Heard Sri. Ganesha R., learned counsel appearing for the appellant/petitioner, Sri. E.I. Sanmathi,
learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company/respondent No.2 and perused the Tribunal records.
10.

Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is not adequate and it has not considered the evidence in the proper perspective and the evidence of the medical officer who has assessed the disability at 52%.
It is contended that the income of the petitioner is not properly considered and global compensation has been awarded by the tribunal without giving sufficient reasons.
It is submitted that the tribunal should have awarded the compensation amount by adopting the structured formula.

The failure on the part of the tribunal has resulted in miscarriage of justice and therefore, reassessment of the compensation amount has Dinesh Poojary vs Jailpuddin S on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142092064/
3 to be done.

sentences.text: 11. The fact that there was an accident involving the two wheeler and lorry owned by respondent No.1/insured and respondent No.2 is not in dispute.
The fact that the petitioner was a pillion rider and that he had suffered injuries is also not in dispute.
The only point to be decided by this Court is regarding the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
It is in this background that the evidence has to be considered by this Court.
12. The petitioner claims that he was doing Centering work and earning Rs.500/- per day and he was also a paper agent at Manipal Media and Network earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Evidently there is absolutely no documentary evidence on record to show the income of the petitioner.
Though the Tribunal considers the contentions of the appellant, it fails to note and conclude as to what is the notional income of the petitioner.
Para 13 of the impugned judgment shows that it has decided the compensation on all the heads in a global manner and without averting to the income of the petitioner and his age.
A perusal of the records disclose that there is no documentary evidence which is available in respect of the income of the petitioner.
As a result, the notional income of the petitioner has to be considered by this Court and the same is held to be Rs.8,500/- per month in view of the guidelines issued by the KSLSA in this regard.

13. So far as the disability of the petitioner is concerned, the evidence of the PW.2 coupled with the treatment certificate produced at Ex.P.13 and the disability certificate produced at Ex.P.16 would reveal that the petitioner had sustained following injuries: (i) open fracture of the right distal humerus (ii) right olecranon fracture (iii) Both bone fracture of the right forearm (iv) Right femur shaft fracture (v) Right proximal tibia fracture.
(vi) Left proximal tibia fracture (vii) Bone deep soft tissue injury of the right foot and liver laceration.
These injuries were treated at Kasturba hospital, Manipal and he was admitted on 03.01.2014 and was discharged on 22.01.2014.
Discharge summary at Ex.P.14 narrates the details of the treatment given to him.
Further he was inpatient from 04.02.2014 and discharged on 10.02.2014.

As may be seen from Ex.P.15, owing to such injuries, the treated doctor has been examined as PW.2 and disability certificate as well as his evidence shows that the petitioner has 24%
disability in his right upper limb and 28% disability in his right lower limb.
He has also found that there is need for a sum of Rs.35,000/- towards the cost of the removal of the implants.

When we consider the above evidence of PW.2 on record con-jointly with the evidence that he was a building worker, it is evident that the disability definitely affects the functional ability as well as economic condition of the petitioner.
In the considered opinion of this Court the functional disability of the petitioner is 19%.
In the light of these conclusions, future loss of income of the petitioner would come to Rs.8,500/- X 12X 16X 19%= 3,10,000/- by adopting the multiplier of '16' for the age of 34 years.
The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards conveyance and incidental expenses.

It is relevant to note that the petitioner was inpatient on two occasions which was spread over more Dinesh Poojary vs Jailpuddin S on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142092064/
4 than 20 days.
Therefore, it would be just and proper to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
15. The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period.

Nature of injuries suggest that the petitioner was unable to resume his work for a period of 4 months and therefore, loss of income for a period of 4 months (Rs.8,500X 4)= Rs.34,000/- has to be awarded.
16.

It is relevant to note that the tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head of the amenities in life and global compensation was awarded by the tribunal including the loss of future earning.

The compensation having been awarded under the future loss of income and nominal amount has to be awarded for the - 11 - loss of amenities in life and therefore, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
17. So far as the compensation under the head of future medical expenses is concerned, the tribunal has totally ignored this aspect despite there being a categorical evidence by PW.2.
Hence, a sum of Rs.35,000/- is awarded as stated by him.
18. There is no need for reassessment of the compensation under the heads of medical expenses and pain and suffering.

19. Hence, the compensation is reassessed as below:
1 Pain and suffering Rs. 1,00,000/-

2 Loss of future income Rs. 3,10,000/-
3

Medical Expenses Rs. 4,11,068/-
4 Loss of income during laid up period Rs. 34,000/- 5 Loss of future comforts and amenities Rs. 25,000/- 6 Conveyance and incidental expenses Rs. 40,000/- 7

Future medical expenses Rs 35,000/-
 Total Rs. 9,55,068/-
 Less: awarded by the Tribunal Rs. 7,61,068/-
 Enhancement Rs. 1,94,000/-
- 12 - Dinesh Poojary vs Jailpuddin S on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142092064/
Thus, the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs.1,94,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part (ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 06.10.2016 passed in MVC No.347/2014 by the Tribunal is modified by enhancing the compensation of Rs.1,94,000/- together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment.

(ii) Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount including the enhanced compensation together with interest within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
- 13 -  (iii) The other conditions and  apportionment remain unaltered.
